title: Pontotoc County drops off Mississippi’s burn-ban map after Friday’s expiration date
excerpt: The state map still marks Lee, Chickasaw and Calhoun counties. The latest drought figures put more than a fifth of Pontotoc County in exceptional drought.
locality: Pontotoc County and neighboring Lee, Chickasaw and Calhoun counties, Mississippi.

paragraphs.text: Pontotoc County was off the Mississippi Forestry Commission’s county burn-ban map Sunday morning. The commission had previously listed the order through Friday, Nov. 20. Its policy sets expiration at midnight on the date listed.

The change stops at the county line. The commission still marks Lee County to the east and Chickasaw and Calhoun counties to the south. Residents with questions about a new Pontotoc County order can reach the Board of Supervisors at 662-489-3900. The commission says county boards generally request bans and the agency approves them.

Dry conditions persist across Pontotoc County. In the Nov. 17 U.S. Drought Monitor figures, 22.75% of the county’s land was in exceptional drought, up from 13.36% a week earlier. The share in extreme drought or worse reached 87.77%. The state map tracks county orders, while the drought figures describe conditions on the ground.
